ZERO NEW IDEAS TODAY. All 14 recommendations are updates to open positions — six closes and eight holds. Do not read 14 rows as 14 fresh opportunities; nothing on this page is new risk. Two causes, both recorded in the notes: the earnings calendar from Oct 1 to Oct 9 is genuinely empty of large-cap catalysts (Q3 season does not open until Oct 15), and the one clean new expression found — a short of the staples/duration complex (XLP) — was blocked by the 3-idea correlation cap, because the book already carries four live bets on the same driver (XLU short open; IYR, TLT and ITB shorts awaiting entry). Being over the cap is itself the finding, and it is why nothing was added rather than a reason to add anyway.

SIX CLOSES NEED AN ORDER AT TODAY'S OPEN, and they are named here in plain words because the enforcement pass demotes an idea with no entry target and no stop to the watchlist — which is correct for a new idea and wrong for an exit. SELL TO CLOSE: NKE, LULU, LCII, BCC, SNX, DINO. NKE is the time-critical one: it reports tonight after the close (2026-10-01, ~16:20 ET, consensus EPS 0.4364 on 11.429B revenue), the long carries no stop, and the stale 38.40 exit decided on 2026-09-08 sits 8.5% above the market and will not fill. Sell at the open, before the print. LULU's stale 100.61 exit has likewise sat unfilled for 22 days at 4.6% above market.

The operative criterion for closing was STOP QUALITY, NOT THESIS QUALITY. NKE, LULU, LCII and BCC carry no stop at all, so their losses are unbounded; SNX (1.38 ATR) and DINO (1.86 ATR) carry stops inside the 2.0 ATR floor, and both only ever cleared reward-to-risk because of that — recomputed at an honest 2.0 ATR stop SNX falls to 1.44 and DINO to 1.95, failing the 2.0 swing floor. A filled position's entry cannot be amended, so the honest resolution is to close rather than re-paper. DINO is closed while trending well and that is stated as probably wrong on the trade and right on the process; BCC is marked the thinnest of the six (-3.1%, still 14.1% above its low).

REWARD-TO-RISK CLUSTERING — read this before sizing. Five of the eight holds land just above their floor: XLU 2.07, XLE 2.13, CEG 2.18, EEM 2.27, GDX 2.28 against a 2.0 swing floor. That cluster is the signature of levels fitted to clear the bar. The mitigating fact is that these are inherited levels from the days each position was published, not numbers set today, and every ratio here was recomputed from the filled entry, the standing target and the standing stop rather than carried over from the notes. It is still the pattern worth distrusting, and GDX in particular passes its ATR floor at 1.83 against 1.80 — a bare pass, flagged in its own row as the first thing to cut.

SYSTEMATIC READ ON THE BOOK: of 14 long positions, 11 sit below both their 20-day and 50-day moving averages, and four are within ~4% of their own 150-day low. Only PFE and EEM are in confirmed uptrends. The book is long a basket of still-falling knives, which is the same thing the track record says from the other side (stock 0/6 to target, avg -5.0%). That raised today's bar against adding another pullback long; it did not ban the category, because 11 closed trades is below the ~15 noise floor.

market_context.summary: Rates are the whole story and the duration complex is being repriced on them. The fetched 10-year is 5.26% against a 3.88% effective fed funds rate — 138bp of term premium — with the 2-year at 4.89% and the 10y-2y spread at +0.41. Long-end yields that high against policy that low is a fiscal/term-premium regime, not a growth regime, and it argues against long duration and against bond-proxy equities. The 2026-09-30 session showed exactly that split: XLP -1.53%, XLV -1.35%, XLF -1.13%, IYR -1.12% and TLT -0.58% to a new 150-day low of 77.55, against QQQ +0.25% and SPY -0.21%. Inside the power complex the growth and bond-proxy legs separated: CEG -3.99% while XLU fell only 0.68%. Index and VIX levels are unavailable this run and are read through ETF proxies only. The catalyst calendar is genuinely empty — NKE tonight is the last large-cap of the August-quarter tail, and Q3 season does not open until Oct 15.

recommendations.thesis: This is an UPDATE to the open XLU short (opened 2026-09-24 at 39.60, now 39.44, +0.4% in favour) and it is the one idea in the book the macro data confirms directly rather than by inference. The mechanism is arithmetic: a regulated utility is valued on its dividend yield against the risk-free rate, and the fetched 10-year is 5.26% while the effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, a 138bp term premium. At that long-end level a low-growth 3-4% yielder must re-rate lower, and it is: XLU closed 9/30 at 39.44, 1.05% off its 150-day low of 39.03, -17.5% off its high of 47.80, below SMA20 (41.28) and SMA50 (42.93). The stop at 40.95 is 2.35 ATR from entry on a fetched ATR14 of 0.575, against the 1.8 ATR ETF floor, and reward-to-risk is (39.60-36.80)/(40.95-39.60) = 2.07.
recommendations.key_risk: The whole position is one bet on the long end staying high, and the same bet is on in three other places awaiting entry (IYR short, TLT short, ITB short), so this report is already over the 3-idea correlation cap on a single driver — if the 10-year mean-reverts toward the policy rate, four ideas lose together. This is also a short that requires margin, and shorting a defensive sector 1% off its low means the easy part of the move has happened: 2.80 of target against 1.35 of risk is being asked for from an already-extended level.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that utilities are no longer a pure bond proxy because datacenter and electrification load growth has turned them into a growth sector, so the yield-versus-rates arithmetic no longer governs them. That objection is real and it is answered inside this report own book: the growth-utility leg and the bond-proxy leg have separated. CEG, an independent power producer with AI-datacenter contracting, fell 3.99% on 9/30 and is -23.9% off its high, while XLU fell only 0.68% and grinds to new lows — the two are not trading as one asset. The bond-proxy weight in XLU is being repriced on rates regardless of what the load-growth names do, which is exactly the split the position relies on.

The stop at 63.00 is 2.60 from entry against a fetched ATR14 of 1.1065, so 2.35 ATR against the 1.8 ATR ETF floor, and reward-to-risk from entry is (71.50-65.60)/(65.60-63.00) = 2.27. The structural risk is the dollar: UUP closed at 28.77 and rose 0.07% on 9/30, and with the US 10-year at 5.26% the carry argument favours the dollar, which is the standard mechanism by which emerging-market equity returns are taken away. A thesis whose transmission channel is not transmitting is not yet a reason to close a working position — but it is a reason not to add, and it is why this is conviction 3.

recommendations.thesis: This is an UPDATE to the open CEG position (opened 2026-08-21 at 272.00, now 254.02, -6.6%) and the recommendation is hold-unchanged with an explicit admission attached. The position survives on stop quality for the same reason CCJ does: the 250.00 stop is 22.00 from entry against a fetched ATR14 of 9.5828, so 2.30 ATR against the 2.0 stock floor, and reward-to-risk from entry is (320.0-272.00)/(272.00-250.00) = 2.18. CEG also still sits 11.1% above its 150-day low of 228.63, the widest low-cushion of any underwater long in the book. The thesis is dispatchable nuclear generation contracted to datacenter load, which is a different asset from a regulated bond-proxy utility — and the 9/30 tape supports that distinction even while hurting the position, since CEG fell 3.99% on a day XLU fell only 0.68%.
recommendations.key_risk: I could not establish WHY CEG fell 3.99% on 2026-09-30 — I did not fetch news or filings for it inside the research budget, so the move is unexplained rather than explained-and-dismissed. That is the material risk here: a 4% single-session break on an unknown cause could be a lost PPA, a regulatory ruling or an outage, any of which would invalidate the thesis rather than merely dent it. The position is also only 1.58% above its stop, or 0.42 ATR, so one more ordinary session resolves it. Treat the hold as provisional on that unexamined gap, and do not size up.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against holding is that this report is simultaneously short XLU and long CEG, which is close to being long and short the same sector, and that the 9/30 session — where CEG fell six times as much as XLU — says the market is treating the AI-power premium as the thing being sold, not the bond-proxy yield. That is the sharper version of the objection and it is only half answerable: the separation of the two legs is exactly what the XLU short relies on, so the split is consistent, but the direction of the split on 9/30 went against CEG rather than for it. Hence conviction 3, a hold with no add, and an explicit instruction not to tighten the stop into the break.

catalyst.event: Crude firming into the Q3 reporting window while energy equities lag it — XLE is the laggard leg of a spread the tape opened on 9/30
catalyst.action: HOLD the existing position with the 60.80 stop UNCHANGED. Do not add here and do not tighten the stop; the level is 2.47 ATR from entry and is doing its job.

recommendations.thesis: This is an UPDATE to the open XLE position (opened 2026-08-15 at 63.90, now 61.50, -3.8%) and the recommendation is to hold it unchanged, which is a decision rather than a default. The stop at 60.80 is 2.47 ATR from entry against a 1.8 ATR floor for an ETF, so it is honestly set, and reward-to-risk from entry is (70.50-63.90)/(63.90-60.80) = 2.13, clearing the 2.0 swing floor without any adjustment. The supporting fact is that crude is firm while energy equities are not: USO rose 1.61% on 9/30 to 145.66 and refiner DINO rose 1.64% to 107.32, on a session when SPY fell 0.21% and XLE was flat at 61.50. XLE is holding its 50d SMA (61.98) within 0.8%.
recommendations.key_risk: The honest problem is that the position sits 1.14% above its own stop, or 0.56 ATR, so a single ordinary down session resolves it. That is the arithmetic of a correctly-placed stop on a trade that has moved against you, not a reason to move the stop, but it does mean this position is likely to be closed by the market within days rather than held for weeks. XLE is also below its SMA20 (63.68), so the near-term trend is against the position even though the 50d holds.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against holding is a negative divergence read: if crude is up 1.61% and the energy equity complex does not follow, that is distribution rather than a spread to be long the cheap leg of, and the 9/30 session is evidence the equities do not believe the crude move. It is answered partially rather than fully — refiners did follow, with DINO up 1.64% to 107.32 and sitting 128% above its 150-day low and above its 50d SMA (98.45), so the non-confirmation is specific to the integrated and E&P weight in XLE rather than to energy as a whole. That is a real weakening of the thesis, which is why this is a hold-with-no-add at conviction 3 rather than an add.

evidence.detail: Fetched ATR14 1.2569; the 60.80 stop is 3.10 from the 63.90 entry = 2.47 ATR against the 1.8 ATR ETF floor. Close 61.50, SMA50 61.9762 (holding within 0.8%), SMA20 63.68, 150-day range 52.62-66.17
Crude-vs-equity divergence measured on the 2026-09-30 session: USO +1.61% to 145.66 and DINO +1.64% to 107.32 against SPY -0.21% and XLE flat at 61.50

The distribution/non-confirmation objection is answered only in part, and the partial answer is stated as such: refiners did confirm the crude move (DINO +1.64%, above its SMA50 of 98.4476) while the broader XLE weight did not
